subject.title: enhancement: Optimize voice message processing pipeline for Telegram

question: What Telegram voice pipeline contract should OpenClaw support before implementation: narrow feedback improvements, async/background TTS delivery, a priority voice lane, or a full staged STT/TTS pipeline with state snapshots?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the requested fix crosses Telegram ingress ordering, STT provider behavior, TTS delivery semantics, caching policy, and session-state visibility, so automation should not choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Design measured staged pipeline
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker, use narrower issues for typing and delivery-mode slices, and require live benchmarks plus state snapshots before coding the async STT/TTS pipeline.

options.title: Limit scope to near-term UX
options.body: Treat immediate typing cues and a separate text-plus-voice delivery policy as the near-term work while leaving priority queues, streaming, and caching unplanned for now.

options.title: Defer broad pipeline work
options.body: Keep current provider tuning and delivery semantics as supported until stronger live evidence shows a staged voice pipeline is worth the complexity.

recommendation.title: Design measured staged pipeline
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker, use narrower issues for typing and delivery-mode slices, and require live benchmarks plus state snapshots before coding the async STT/TTS pipeline.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across Telegram audio auto-transcription and TTS runtime behavior.
